request.spec:
The sheets of a tree now share one sheet-wide number sequence: a claim opened on any sheet of the
tree receives the next number after the last number given anywhere in the tree (numbers given before
this stay as they are). Per-period numbering stays per sheet.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The sheets of a tree now share one sheet-wide number sequence: a claim opened on any sheet of the

agent.result_text:
All the sheets in a tree now share one claim number sequence. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec. I ran it before my last edit, which only changed a code comment.

**What changed** (server only, in `SheetService.nextClaimNumber`):
- When a claim is opened, the app follows the parent links up to the tree's top sheet, then collects that sheet and every sheet below it.
- The new number is one more than the highest number given on any of those sheets, and is stored as the opening sheet's last number.
- Numbers already given stay as they are. In the test, after linking a sheet to a parent that both already had a 1, the next claim on either became 2, and the numbers went on from there across the tree.
- Per-period numbering (`P1-1`, `X-1`) still counts per sheet, as before.
- Two claims opened at the same moment anywhere in the tree can't get the same number: the tree's top sheet stays locked until the opening is saved.

No database migration was needed, because each sheet's existing "last number given" counter now holds the tree-wide number. In `SheetRepository` I replaced the old "add one to this sheet's counter" queries with "set the counter" and "highest counter among these sheets". I also updated the comment on `ClaimService.nextNumber` to match.

**One risk:**
- **Rare deadlock:** a claim moved by transfer or clone into another sheet of the same tree, while someone opens a claim on that sheet, could deadlock. The two actions lock the same two sheets in opposite orders, and one would fail when the database times it out. The tests don't cover this.
